resources.string: Check the following before starting the dissection procedure.
Dissecting instruments: scalpel, forceps, scissors, pins
This system\'s interactive atlas has not been migrated to the native app yet (Phase 2). Nothing has been substituted in its place.
Tap a marker or a structure name to inspect the anatomy.
Pinch to zoom • drag to pan • double-tap to reset
This raster plate is a visual reference. Structure touch targets remain on the interactive SVG atlas until raster coordinates are independently calibrated and verified.
Use this plate for visual recognition. Segment spacing is schematic; the interactive structure text remains the evidence-aware source for pore positions, setae and specimen variation.

Visual reference plate. The printed segment labels retain the source file’s teaching convention. The interactive text records specimen evidence reporting gizzard IX–X and caecal origin XXVII, so do not treat the raster labels as universal species characters.

Connection-focused reference plate. The VII/IX/XII/XIII four-pair heart map is retained as the practical teaching convention used by the source application; consult the structure text for provenance and specimen-level cautions.
Teaching enlargement: tissue thickness and vessel spacing are deliberately exaggerated. The physiological direction of gas exchange is the teaching focus.
Nephridial units are enlarged and spaced schematically for recognition. Use the interactive text for category definitions, drainage type and segment-specific evidence.
Paired organs are enlarged and separated for visibility; relative organ size and spacing are not to scale. Use the interactive labels for exact teaching positions.
The plate emphasizes topology and continuity of the nerve ring and ventral cord. Relative dimensions are enlarged for teaching.
Use the high-resolution transverse section as a visual recognition plate; confirm tissue relationships and named structures with the interactive atlas and reviewed structure text.
